PEP-adjacent flag: Markus Braun was listed from 2017 as member of the Staff Unit for Strategy, Analysis and Planning of Austrian Chancellor Sebastian Kurz; Chancellery spokesperson later said he had not worked in the unit
PEP flag: James H. Freis Jr. is a former senior public official (Director of US Treasury FinCEN, 2007–2012); former-PEP review flagged, current statutory PEP status not established
Law-enforcement listing (not a sanctions designation): Jan Marsalek is subject to an INTERPOL red notice for fraud and listed among Germany BKA wanted fugitives
Adverse media: From April 2015 to 2019 FT Alphaville/FT investigations raised accounting-fraud allegations about Wirecard, which the company denied; later confirmed after the 2020 collapse

Adverse media: KPMG special audit could not verify majority of 2016–2018 profits; EY failed to verify cash reserves in apparently fraudulent bank statements; BaFin referred misleading investor statements to prosecutors

Adverse media: June 2020 Wirecard admitted €1.9bn in cash missing, shares fell almost 90%, EY refused to sign off accounts; on 2020-06-25 Wirecard AG applied for insolvency proceedings at Munich Local Court
Adverse media: Markus Braun detained 22 June 2020 on suspicion of accounting fraud and market manipulation, released on €5m bail

Adverse media: 2020-07-22 Munich prosecutors announced arrests of former Wirecard executives (Braun re-arrested) alleging fabricated third-party-acquirer business and assets to obtain approx. EUR 3.2bn financing, EUR 1.9bn allegedly nonexistent assets; allegations against individuals, not a corporate conviction
Adverse media: Jan Marsalek fled Germany, reportedly in Russia; British authorities (Met Police, March 2025) describe him as a Russian spy with GRU links
Adverse media: BaFin supervisory failure over Wirecard; Bundestag inquiry announced 1 Sept 2020; BaFin president Felix Hufeld and deputy Elisabeth Roegele left 29 Jan 2021
Adverse media: Administrator Jaffé dismantled Wirecard from 1 July 2020; main business sold to Santander for €100m in November 2020; ~730 employees laid off

Adverse media: 2020-08-25 Munich Local Court opened insolvency proceedings over Wirecard AG (illiquidity and over-indebtedness) and appointed Michael Jaffé; scandalous circumstances referenced; administration ongoing
Adverse media: March 2022 Munich prosecutors charged Markus Braun with fraud, breach of trust and accounting manipulation (up to 15 years); Braun denies wrongdoing

Adverse media: Trial opened 8 December 2022 in Munich; Braun, Bellenhaus and von Erffa face commercial gang fraud charges for falsifying financial statements since 2015, causing €3.1bn loss to banks; verdict expected 2026 or 2027

Adverse media: 2023-12-14 prosecutors announced indictment of former CFO for alleged false reporting, market manipulation, commercial gang fraud, embezzlement and related assistance; allegations remain to be proved

Adverse media: 2024-08-06 Munich prosecutors charged former CFO Alexander von Knoop and former CPO Susanne Steidl with several counts of embezzlement (von Knoop also with aiding embezzlement); alleged losses of several hundred million euros; decision on trial pending

Adverse media: 5 Sept 2024 Munich Regional Court I ordered former Wirecard management board members incl. Braun and former CFO to pay EUR 140m plus interest for breaches of duty (Marsalek already under partial default judgment for EUR 140m); supervisory-board claim failed for lack of causality

Adverse media: 2025-11-13 Federal Court of Justice ruled Wirecard AG shareholders' capital-markets damages claims are not ordinary insolvency claims and rank behind ordinary creditors; approx. EUR 15.4bn claims filed vs approx. EUR 650m assets; court described allegations that Wirecard feigned its business model

Adverse media: 2026-10-08 Munich court rejected defence request to suspend and restart the Wirecard fraud trial of Braun and co-defendants; closing arguments targeted for November; Braun denies accusations; no final verdict

c1.note: GLEIF legal name is Wirecard AG.

c2.note: GLEIF registeredAs is HRB 169227, with registration authority RA000304 (Amtsgericht München). The GLEIF record does not name the court, so the München part rests on the registry authority code.

c3.note: LEI matches. Entity status is ACTIVE, registration status is LAPSED, and last update is 2020-11-13.

c4.note: GLEIF jurisdiction is DE. The legal address is Einsteinring 35, Aschheim.

c5.note: Wikipedia gives a founding date of 1 Jan 1999, but the registered entity HRB 169227 is the former InfoGenie AG, renamed in the 2005 reverse merger. GLEIF has creationDate null. I could not confirm 1999-01-01 as the legal incorporation date of this entity.

c6.note: GLEIF has creationDate null, so it gives no 2000-06-20 date. The Handelsregister page shows HRB 169227 entered 06.08.2007.

c7.note: The GLEIF legal address is Einsteinring 35, 85609 Aschheim. The record is lapsed and was last updated in 2020, so the address is out of date.

c8.note: Entry no. 29 of 27.06.2022 changed the business address to Humboldtstraße 8, 85609 Aschheim.

c9.note: The register shows insolvency proceedings opened 25.08.2020 and the company dissolved as a result, which fits the status. The claim that the core business was sold to Santander in November 2020 is, as far as I recall, inaccurate. I did not check the Wikipedia page or confirm this by search.

c10.note: Wirecard Acceptance Technologies GmbH appears in a list of Wirecard entities. I found no record of HRB 238107 or of its subsidiary link to Wirecard AG.

c11.note: North Data confirms HRB 223366, Amtsgericht München, listed as in liquidation, and it was among the Wirecard group companies in insolvency.

c12.note: I found no source tying HRB 235570 to this company, and none confirming its liquidation status.

c13.note: The company is confirmed as insolvent (filed 8 July 2020, business sold to Unzer POS), but I found no source for HRB 143760.

c14.note: The company is confirmed as insolvent in 2020, but I found no source for HRB 200352.

c15.note: HRB 24925 at Amtsgericht Leipzig matches. It was a Wirecard subsidiary, insolvent from 2020, and sold to IDnow.

c16.note: The Jaffé page names him insolvency administrator of Wirecard AG, with proceedings opened 25.08.2020 by Amtsgericht München. The page gives no separate appointment date, so the date is inferred from the opening of proceedings.

c17.note: Wikipedia confirms he was CEO/CTO from January 2002, resigned 19 June 2020, was dismissed 30 June 2020, and is Austrian.

c18.note: Wikipedia says he held more than 7% and was the largest single shareholder. He cut the stake to about 2.5% in June 2020.

c19.note: Wikipedia confirms COO from 1 Feb 2010, Asia business, dismissal 18 June 2020, born in Vienna and listed as Austrian. Later reports of Russian citizenship do not change the Austrian listing.

c20.note: He was Wirecard AG's CFO and board member, and Reuters reports he was charged in 2024. I could not fetch Reuters and did not check the register page. The claim is about a past role and already says current appointment is unverified, so it stands as written.

c21.note: Mondaq confirms he was appointed interim CEO on 19 June 2020 and was a former FinCEN director and Deutsche Börse Group CCO. The register shows an entry dated 1 July 2020. The article does not give his nationality. He is not in the current active list, but the claim already says current appointment is not verified.

c22.note: The register lists her on the management board from March 2018. Reuters-based reports call her the board member for product development, and Fintelegram calls her chief product officer.

c23.note: Mondaq states he was an independent Supervisory Board member and Chairman since January 2020.

c24.note: The cited URL returned 404 without the www prefix. Search results for the working URL say he is the former head of Wirecard's Dubai subsidiary, a co-defendant in the Munich trial and the key prosecution witness.

c25.note: Search results for the working URL describe him as the former chief accountant and a co-defendant in the Munich trial.

c26.note: Wikipedia says he was a member of the Kurz Staff Unit from 2017, and a Chancellery spokesperson later said he had not worked there since the government took office.

c27.note: The Treasury release confirms his 2007 appointment as FinCEN Director. The end of his tenure in 2012 comes from general knowledge, not this page. The claim already says current PEP status is not established.

c28.note: OpenSanctions lists Marsalek under INTERPOL Red Notices and Germany BKA Wanted Fugitives. The search page does not show the notice details, and it matches the claim's framing as a law-enforcement listing rather than a sanctions designation.

c29.note: The FT's 2015 reporting is supported, and Wirecard's denial of later allegations is supported (it sued the FT in 2019). The article does not say the company denied the 2015 report specifically. The April 2015 FT Alphaville start date and the denial are consistent with what I know, but I did not confirm them on a page.

c30.note: The article supports the KPMG and EY findings. Misleading statements made during the special audit led to a BaFin complaint to prosecutors.

c31.note: The article confirms €1.9bn missing and the 25 June 2020 insolvency filing. I did not find the ~90% share fall or EY refusing sign-off on the page; both are widely reported and the claim is broadly accurate.

c32.note: Braun was detained 22 June 2020 on suspicion of accounting fraud and market manipulation, then released on €5m bail on 23 June.

c33.note: The 22 July 2020 Munich prosecutors' release confirms the arrests, about €3.2bn of financing, and up to €1.9bn of allegedly nonexistent assets. These are allegations against individuals.

c34.note: I could not open the Reuters page. Wikipedia confirms Marsalek fled (it says to Belarus), and the GRU link is widely reported from the March 2025 UK spy-ring case, so I treat the claim as accurate.

c35.note: The article confirms the Bundestag inquiry announced 1 Sept 2020 and the departure of Hufeld and Roegele on 29 Jan 2021.

c36.note: Wikipedia confirms about 730 staff cut in August 2020 and the core business sold to Santander for €100m in November 2020. The '1 July 2020' start date was not checked against a source.

c37.note: The Munich Local Court press release shows proceedings opened for Wirecard AG on 25.08.2020 (1542 IN 1308/20) with Jaffé appointed administrator. The Eröffnungsbeschluss PDF returned empty, so the 'illiquidity and over-indebtedness' grounds were not confirmed.

c38.note: The page confirms Braun was charged in March 2022. The 15-year maximum and Braun's denial were not seen on the page.

c39.note: The article, found under a corrected URL, confirms the trial began in December 2022 with Braun, Bellenhaus and von Erffa as defendants and a verdict expected in 2026 or 2027. The €3.1bn bank loss was not found in the search results.

c40.note: The prosecutors' release confirms an indictment dated 12 Dec 2023 against the former finance chief. Charges are false reporting, market manipulation, commercial gang fraud, breach of trust and aiding; facts still to be proven. The 14 Dec announcement date was not checked.

c41.field: adverse_media: 2024 charges von Knoop and Steidl
c41.note: Reuters-based reports confirm the 6 Aug 2024 embezzlement charges and losses of several hundred million euros. Whether the court would admit the case was still open. I could not open the Reuters page itself.

c42.note: Baker McKenzie and news reports confirm the 5 Sep 2024 Munich judgment (5 HK O 17452/21). It ordered Braun, the former CPO and the former CFO to pay EUR 140m plus interest, and Klestil, a supervisory-board member, was not held liable. I could not retrieve the supervisory-board causality reasoning or the Marsalek default-judgment detail.

c43.field: adverse_media: 2025 BGH ruling on shareholder claims
c43.note: The BGH ruled on 13 Nov 2025 (IX ZR 127/24) that shareholders' capital-market damages claims are not ordinary insolvency claims. The BGH press release was unreachable, so the 'feigned business model' wording is unchecked.

c44.note: Handelsblatt, 8 Oct 2026, confirms the court refused to suspend the trial, closing arguments are targeted for November, Braun denies all allegations, and there is no verdict yet.

c12.note: Northdata lists Wirecard Issuing Technologies GmbH, Aschheim, Munich District Court HRB 235570, status liquidation, with Wirecard AG as shareholder.

c20.note: Alexander von Knoop was CFO and a management board member of Wirecard AG (HRB 169227). Reuters reported in 2024 that he was charged. Not re-fetched in this run.

c25.note: Stephan von Erffa was Wirecard AG's chief accountant and is a co-defendant with Braun and Bellenhaus in Munich. The cited Börsen-Zeitung URL returns 404; the article exists at /english/ and was confirmed through search.

c30.note: Matches well-known reporting summarized on Wikipedia: KPMG could not verify 2016–18 profits, EY failed to verify cash in forged bank statements, and BaFin filed a criminal complaint over misleading statements. The Wikipedia page was not re-fetched in this run.

c37.note: EQS notice confirms the Munich court opened insolvency proceedings over Wirecard AG and appointed Michael Jaffé. The 25 Aug 2020 date and the stated grounds are from general knowledge; the court order PDF was not fetched.

c39.note: Trial opened 8 Dec 2022 on commercial gang fraud charges. The Börsen-Zeitung article put the verdict in 2026, possibly 2027. €3.1bn is the indictment's figure (from memory, not confirmed here). Oct 2026 reports say closing pleas are expected in November, so the timeline is outdated.

c40.note: Munich I prosecutors' release of 14 Dec 2023: former CFO 'L.' (Burkhard Ley) indicted for false reporting, market manipulation, commercial gang fraud, breach of trust and aiding. 'Embezzlement' is a loose translation of Untreue.
